chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Furat, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said:

Indeed, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) is the vicegerent of God and my vicegerent, the proof of God and my proof, the gate of God and my gate, the elect of God and my elect, the beloved of God and my beloved, the friend of God and my friend, and the sword of God and my sword. He is my brother, my companion, my vizier, and my deputy. His lovers are my lovers, his haters are my haters, his supporters are my supporters, his enemies are my enemies, his war is my war, his peace is my peace, his word is my word, his command is my command, his wife is my daughter, his descendants are my descendants, and he is the Master of Deputies and the best of my entire nation.

key_terms.حجة: Proof, the divine proof through whom God's guidance is established
key_terms.خليفة: Vicegerent, successor, one appointed to represent authority on behalf of another
key_terms.سيد الوصيين: Master of the Deputies; a title affirming Ali's preeminence among all prophetic successors
key_terms.صفي: Elect, chosen one; denotes special selection by God
key_terms.وصي: Deputy, executor of a will; in Shia theology, the designated successor of a Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about the status of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Imam al-Baqir (AS) and the Ahl al-Bayt chain, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) enumerates the unique spiritual and temporal stations of Imam Ali (AS). Using a series of paired declarations linking Ali to both God and himself, the Prophet establishes Ali's role as his rightful successor, representative, and spiritual heir. This hadith was recorded in the assembly of Sheikh al-Saduq in Muharram 368 AH, during a period when establishing the theological basis of Imamate was central to Shia scholarly activity.
